lessons.title: website

explanation.title: anchor
explanation.text: export default async function HomePage

explanation.title: why
explanation.text: Next.js uses app/page.tsx to build the home page. HomePage prepares what visitors see; async lets it wait for data before composing the page.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: Without a page at this route, Next.js would not know what home screen to render. This file arranges the display; it does not replace the database.

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: async / await

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: A function can wait for work to finish, such as loading products.

lessons.why: Next.js uses app/page.tsx to build the home page. HomePage prepares what visitors see; async lets it wait for data before composing the page.

explanation.title: anchor
explanation.text: return Math.max(

explanation.title: why
explanation.text: This function totals shipping, fees, taxes and discounts. minorUnits works in cents to limit rounding errors; / 100 converts back to currency units.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: Duplicating this calculation across pages risks inconsistent totals. Math.max(0, …) prevents a negative discounted total.

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: Use zero when a value is missing (null or undefined).

lessons.title: react

explanation.title: anchor
explanation.text: export default function CollectionProductCard

explanation.title: why
explanation.text: A product card is a reusable React component. It receives product as input: the same presentation can show different names, images and prices.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: Writing every card by hand makes fixes slow and inconsistent. A component lets one change improve every card.

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: props

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: Information passed into a component, such as product here.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: You would need a separate page per product. A dynamic route shares the template while giving each product its own URL.

lessons.title: api

explanation.title: anchor
explanation.text: export async function GET(req: NextRequest)

explanation.title: why
explanation.text: GET is a read request. This route receives it, reads parameters and prepares product data. route.ts handles data; page.tsx builds a page.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: The page would need another way to request server data. An API provides a contract: a defined request and an expected response.

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: GET

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: An HTTP method used to request information.

lessons.why: GET is a read request. This route receives it, reads parameters and prepares product data. route.ts handles data; page.tsx builds a page.

lessons.title: database

explanation.title: anchor
explanation.text: const url = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;

explanation.title: why
explanation.text: This code reads configuration and prepares the server connection to Supabase. process.env reads an environment variable, not product data.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: Without a valid URL and key, the server cannot use this database client. The service key must stay on the server, never in the browser.

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: variable d’environnement / environment variable

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: A setting supplied to a program separately from its code.

lessons.why: This code reads configuration and prepares the server connection to Supabase. process.env reads an environment variable, not product data.

lessons.title: security

explanation.title: anchor
explanation.text: async function requireOwner

explanation.title: why
explanation.text: The server checks identity and role before allowing owner access. This runs even when someone calls the API without using its button.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: Hiding a screen is not enough: someone could call its API directly. Permission checks belong on the server.

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: 401: identity not authenticated. 403: access forbidden.

lessons.why: The server checks identity and role before allowing owner access. This runs even when someone calls the API without using its button.

lessons.title: orders

explanation.title: anchor
explanation.text: export async function POST(req: NextRequest)

explanation.title: why
explanation.text: POST sends a request that can create an order. The route must check it before saving anything: the browser is not a trusted source of prices.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: Without server checks, edited quantities or prices could be accepted. Study this code without creating a real order.

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: POST

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: An HTTP method for sending data to be processed.

lessons.why: POST sends a request that can create an order. The route must check it before saving anything: the browser is not a trusted source of prices.

lessons.title: payments

explanation.title: anchor
explanation.text: if (!(await verifyPayPalWebhook

explanation.title: why
explanation.text: A webhook is a message PayPal sends to the server. This code verifies its signature before trusting it. A success page alone does not prove confirmed payment.

explanation.title: without
explanation.text: A fake message could be mistaken for confirmation. This check rejects an invalid signature before further processing.

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: webhook

explanation.title: vocabulary
explanation.text: A server-to-server notification when an event occurs.

lessons.why: A webhook is a message PayPal sends to the server. This code verifies its signature before trusting it. A success page alone does not prove confirmed payment.
